text.tspan: Page 5, the end of About this release candidate
What the pen says, word for word, and what it means
A RELEASE, NOT A DRAFT
“Not to me [over: Then, if you are Dinis,]
... I am :) [over: read it with a pen]”
The book should not talk to Dinis; it talks to the reader.
(And yes, he is reading it with a pen.)
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“we need to tell the reader that if they are
reading this on a screen they should stop ↓
and print this book”
Tell the reader to print it: the book is meant to be read
on paper.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“here we should have a section pointing to
the website of this book & · show what is
there, namely the tools & visualisations ·
show where to find the chapter PDFs (for
print)”
A section that points to the book's website: what is
there, the tools and visualisations, and the chapter PDFs
for print.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“VERY important → explain that this entire
book content is released under CC-BY which
means they are free to · copy it ·
distribute it · sell it · remix. All they
need to do is to have a small credit of
where the text came from ... CC-BY is a
copyright licence that gives the reader
rights”
Explain CC BY in plain words: copy, distribute, sell,
remix, with a small credit.
THE FIRST PAGES SELL THE BOOK
“page 5 and "why am I reading this book?" +
"why should I continue"”
By page 5 the reader still does not know why to read the
book, or why to go on.
